answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require every agent identity to finish a verifiable delay function before acting each epoch: a sequential computation taking ten minutes that cannot be sped up by running it on many machines in parallel. An attacker spawning a nebula of fake identities must pay that delay for each one in turn, so a fake army grows only at single-clock speed, while honest agents pay it once. This is no fable of perfect security: at the nadir of the scheme, a faster chip still shortens the delay, so it must be re-tuned against current hardware and combined with rate limits.
